Hey @jonathanKingston while doing the final review and testing the app, I noticed an issue with the implementation that I hadn't caught earlier. Every time I launched the App I could see the linear onboarding. It seems the initial below suggestion I made for
```
func startOnboardingFlowIfNotSeenBefore() {
        let forceShowOnboarding = !LaunchOptionsHandler().isOnboardingCompleted
        let showOnboarding = !tutorialSettings.hasSeenOnboarding || forceShowOnboarding
        guard showOnboarding else { return }
        segueToDaxOnboarding()
}
```
had a flaw in this line `let forceShowOnboarding = !LaunchOptionsHandler().isOnboardingCompleted` and I only discovered it today during testing. The reason is that if environment[“ONBOARDING"] and launch arguments for "isOnboardingCompleted” are not set `LaunchOptionsHandler().isOnboardingCompleted` returns false and we force showing the linear onboarding.

I think we need to model the case where we do not override the values and a Bool is not sufficient anymore. 

I had a bit of down time Today so I’ve gone ahead and implemented the necessary changes. I’ve created a [new branch](https://github.com/duckduckgo/apple-browsers/compare/jkt/launch-arguments...alessandro/launch-arguments-fixes?expand=1) off your current branch and pushed the updates there.
If you’re happy with those changes, we can merge them into your branch.

Again, thanks for your work on this, and let me know if you have any questions or want to go over the fix together!

@alessandroboron agreed if we want the force 'on' then tri-state enum makes the most sense. I think it's a little unfortunate to have that go everywhere but I'd like to get my other work unblocked that needs this change.

I am however a little concerned that the .maestro files needed to add isOnboardingCompleted or run  `onboarding.yaml`

As mentioned in MM there are tests that kill and relaunch the App again. In that scenario the onboarding is presented again because the launch argument is not passed to the main application. This causes the tests to fail. The solution is to pass ${ONBOARDING_COMPLETED} in these tests.

BEFORE:
```
- stopApp
- launchApp
```

AFTER:
```
- stopApp
- launchApp:
    arguments:
      isOnboardingCompleted: ${ONBOARDING_COMPLETED}
```

My first thought was to replace `- launchApp` with 

```
runWorkflow:
   file: ../shared/setup.yaml
```

But that workflow reset the state of the app. If the test had a webview open calling setup.yaml would clear everything.


EDIT: @jonathanKingston I pushed other changes to avoid passing the ${ONBOARDING_COMPLETED} variable every time we launch the App. I run the tests locally and they work fine. I’ll run the tests in CI to double check and we can merge the  PR in.

Hey, @afterxleep , looking great so far! Background pause works well as far as I could test it. Since this is still an internal prototype, I don't see any blockers in the JS code, but here are some things we need to consider before going to production:

1. The number of JS files is likely to grow as you add more features and hacks to the webview. We'd need to set up a build process for JS to ensure code quality and backward compatibility. I see rollup already being used for autoconsent in the repo, but since we're bringing in C-S-S already -- which has a decent toolchain behind it -- we should at least look into extracting these JS files into their own C-S-S feature.

2. The mediaControl.js file is clever in how it patches the element's prototype, but like we spoke earlier in the week, it's risky to override methods at that level and probably not effective in the long run as it might turn into a game of cat and mouse. Let's catch up early next week and look at ways to make that script more robust. Shane might have some ideas too.

> "Switch to tab" label in the suggestion row is present if you restore a window and minimise it after. It's not present in next attempts.

Nice catch! I have a fix for this in 327c296. The check for the frame size was happening too soon (and using the frame’s intrinsic width, which is very large) so it was always showing the “Switch to tab” label in a restored window. I updated it so that any time the view is resized it checks again if the label should be shown:

> The options button for bookmarks folder is present on top or left to the bookmark folder icon in the compressed state

This one is a little tricky. The same behavior is present in production, but it requires a lot of nested folders to notice it. The fix in 2c21471 feels a little hacky to me, but it does prevent this overlap with the bookmark folder icon. It doesn’t resolve overlap between the menu button and indentation marker (disclosure icon), which is laid out automatically, and it doesn’t resolve other odd layout issues for very nested folders. Those feel out of scope for this project — they are pre-existing layout issues that are more discoverable with the smaller width, but would require more in-depth investigation and layout changes to fully resolve.

 - `fetch(_:isDebug:)`

When sponsored shortcuts are enabled, we run into a scenario that I believe we’ll have to accept as a slight difference in Firefox vs. our imported shortcuts: * Amazon is one of the sponsored shortcuts for your profile. * When there is a sponsored shortcut, Firefox filters out any frecent sites from the same domain (so a frecent Amazon site won’t appear alongside the sponsored Amazon shortcut; Firefox drops it and you’ll get the next frecent site in that position instead). * When we perform the import, we can’t see what sponsored shortcuts Firefox is using, so we use the frecent sites without any filtering. You’ll get the Amazon frecent site as an imported shortcut, instead of the shortcut Firefox replaced it with. (In this case, the second-to-last shortcut is Amazon instead of dzen.ru.) We didn’t discuss this exact scenario in the ship review, but we did discuss the possibility of some small differences like this and decided it’s worth getting user feedback to see if this is close enough to be a useful/positive experience.

* In that case, if the user has pinned shortcuts in the last 3 spots in the list, they won’t be imported (because we reduce the count by 3 to account for sponsored shortcuts).
* But a pinned shortcut is a signal that it’s important to the user, so it would be better to import it anyway.

Thanks for the review @ayoy!

> This is a really minor thing, but if a crash occurs when user had 1 window with 1 new tab page open, we still ask them to restore open tabs, and if they agree, we open another window with a tab. Should we skip showing the dialog in this case?

We didn’t discuss this exact scenario, but in the kickoff while syncing with the Windows implementation we discussed the overall approach: The plan was to add the check for an unexpected app termination without making any changes to the actual session state restoration logic. In other words, as long as we have a session to restore we’ll offer to restore it, and that includes the 1 window with 1 new tab page scenario since we’re saving that state.

Given the previous discussion I think changing that behavior is out of scope for this project. It could be done as a followup but I also see limited benefit: it seems less likely that the app will close unexpectedly with just the new tab page open, and it doesn’t do much harm to offer the option to restore. We could keep an eye out for complaints about the prompt appearing when it isn’t needed, but otherwise I’d argue the effort isn’t worth the improved behavior.

Thanks for working on this @federicocappelli! Overall I'm happy that we're able to simplify the PixelKit event types down & make the `fire` call simpler, and I think this is a reasonable use of reflection, though there is a part of me that likes having `error` as part of the protocol definition just so that it's crystal clear to someone implementing a new pixel. Assuming we move forward with the reflection approach, I left a comment about making sure the associated-value based API is clear to those using it, but would welcome @diegoreymendez's thoughts.

I also saw two places where we had some `var error` definitions that I don't think are needed any more:
* `SessionRestorePromptPixel`
* `VPNSubscriptionStatusPixel`

@samsymons I cleaned up all remaining `var error: (any Error)?` thanks.

I think the previous API had a few issues:
1. The event and the error creation were disconnected and made at different moments. I didn't find any reason why the error shouldn't be part of the Event signature, like all other parameters. Now, IMO, the PixelKit use is much cleaner and we don't require manual bridges between the Event parameters and the final Error added to the dictionary.
2. The requirement to add the `var error: (any Error)?`, 99% of the time returning nil, to each Event seemed a bit cumbersome. Many Events already had an Error as parameter, the `var error` bridge was just an implementation limitation.
@samsymons  I think I found a solution that satisfies everyone. I re-added the `var error: NSError? { get }` to the PixelKitEvent protocol but it's automatically implemented by the extension, WDYT?
@tomasstrba sure, I’ll handle it!

We discussed the pixel during the kick-off call. We agreed that having a pixel without the input parameter would be non-actionable anyway because we wouldn’t know where are the discrepancies. Also, it’s not that the rust library is a black box, but we’ve implemented it and we tested it with existing macOS and Windows test cases, so the expectation is that it will actually work the same as native implementation. Lastly, the native implementation is not a golden standard, but one another approach at classifying user input, so it’s not a given that it would always be correct, and the pixel sent without an input parameter wouldn’t allow us to tell if that’s a problem with the native mechanism or unified.

> My only thought here is 15 minutes is a lot, and introduces a higher risk the user might kill the app and turn the pixel into an abandoned pixel which gets reported with a different reason.

Yeah, I agree. 15 minutes is quite long for iOS setup flow. But I don’t think it increases the risk of abandoned pixels caused by users killing the app. If the flow completes successfully or fails with an error, the pixel is finalized and sent immediately. The timeout only affects flows that remain in progress beyond that threshold.

> I think it might make sense to reduce this to something like 2 minutes - which should be plenty for the VPN connection.

Yeah, that makes sense. 2 minutes should be more than enough for connection alone, but if we include the setup portion I think around 5 minutes would be safer. The flow can take longer for some users since it involves:
- Toggling on the VPN (fast)
- Prompted to grant configuration permission (takes some thinking time for some users)
- Entering device passcode to add the VPN profile (takes some times for some users - including wrong passcode retries)
- completing setup

> After completing the test case, I reset the prompt and today's date to repeat the test. However, on subsequent runs, the active prompt displays instead of the inactive ones. Am I doing something wrong? See the attached video.

I reproduced this by testing at a time that was earlier in the day than when I first installed the app. It looks like this is an ambiguity in the Calendar extension `numberOfDaysBetween(_:and:)`. That method uses `dateComponents(_:from:to:)` which only counts full days (24 hours) between dates. So if you check the number of days between e.g. Nov 1 at 8PM and Nov 3 at 8AM it only counts 1 day, whereas between Nov 1 at 8AM and Nov 3 at 8PM counts 2 days. On one hand that’s expected (if you expect a day to mean 24 hours) but it’s confusing if you’re only interested in counting calendar days.

In this case, it’s problematic because of how the date is advanced in the debug menu. We add the correct number of days to the install date to give the date that the prompt will be shown. However, if the install date was Nov 1 at 8PM and you are testing at 8AM, the debug menu will give the date as Nov 29 but your override will set the date as Nov 29 at 8AM and the prompt won’t actually be shown until Nov 29 at 8PM.

This is consistent with the popover prompt, as well — I had the same results when I tested that prompt.

**Solutions**

Is this the expected behavior (waiting for X number of full days to pass after install before a prompt will be shown) or do we only care about calendar days? If it’s calendar days, we could normalize it by checking the start of each day, for example:

```swift
let daysSince: (Date?) -> Int = { date in
    guard let date else { return 0 }
    return Calendar.current.numberOfDaysBetween(date.startOfDay, and: dateProvider().startOfDay) ?? 0
}
```

Alternately, if we’re happy with the current behavior then I’d suggest we always use a fresh install of the app when testing these features. That way the install time will be earlier in the day than the override time, so we’ll always be advancing full days from the install. (I can be sure to include that in my testing steps from now on.)

> When the user selects "Never Ask Again," the debug menu still shows the date for the inactive prompt. This is a minor bug in the debug view, but I recommend fixing it to prevent confusion during testing

Thanks @alessandroboron! I considered using all the same pixels, but didn't for a few reasons:

* The implementation request included using the existing pixels, and just adding new pixels as needed.
* We have some dashboards for this already, so the primary need here is to add the new pixels to those dashboards. (It could be more work to replace the existing ones.)
* The existing pixels measure the exact same things (impressions/clicks/dismiss) so if we fire both for the same trigger we're duplicating data and potentially creating confusion if someone sees the two different pixels later on and wonders why we have both.

That said, I agree that consistently triggering the same pixels for all the cards makes more sense if you're just looking at these new pixels, without the past context. I'll go ahead and make that change, and we can decide for each dashboard how to best update it.
